---
title: "Windows: SSH setup"
---

## Setup: SSH

### On Windows 11

Open **PowerShell as Administrator**.

First check/install OpenSSH Server:

```powershell
Get-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Server*
```

If it shows `State : NotPresent`:

```powershell
Get-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Server* |
    Add-WindowsCapability -Online
```

Then enable and start the SSH service:

```powershell
Set-Service -Name sshd -StartupType Automatic
Start-Service sshd
```

Check it:

```powershell
Get-Service sshd
```

You want:

```text
Status   Name
------   ----
Running  sshd
```

Windows' built-in OpenSSH Server is the implementation Ansible recommends for SSH-managed Windows hosts.

### Check port 22 locally

Still on Windows:

```powershell
Test-NetConnection localhost -Port 22
```

You want:

```text
TcpTestSucceeded : True
```

If that is `False`, stop there—the SSH server itself is not working yet.

### Check the firewall

Run:

```powershell
Get-NetFirewallRule |
    Where-Object DisplayName -Like "*OpenSSH*"
```

Normally installing OpenSSH creates the appropriate inbound rule. If you don't see one, create it explicitly:

```powershell
New-NetFirewallRule `
    -Name "sshd-Server-In-TCP" `
    -DisplayName "OpenSSH SSH Server" `
    -Enabled True `
    -Direction Inbound `
    -Protocol TCP `
    -Action Allow `
    -LocalPort 22
```

This matches the setup recommended in the current Ansible Windows SSH documentation.

### Find the Windows IP address

Run:

```powershell
ipconfig
```

Look for the IPv4 address of the active Ethernet/Wi-Fi adapter, for example:

```text
IPv4 Address . . . . . . : 192.168.178.42
```

Also get your Windows username:

```powershell
whoami
```

You might get:

```text
DESKTOP-ABC\gerit
```

Usually the SSH username would then be:

```text
gerit
```

### Test from Linux

From your Fedora/Linux machine:

```bash
ssh gerit@192.168.178.42
```

Replace both values accordingly.

On the first connection you'll probably see:

```text
The authenticity of host ... can't be established.
Are you sure you want to continue connecting?
```

Enter:

```text
yes
```

Then enter your **Windows account password**.

If successful, you'll land in something like:

```text
Microsoft Windows [Version ...]
...
C:\Users\gerit>
```

At this point, **SSH works**.

### Then switch the SSH shell to PowerShell

Ansible recommends PowerShell as the Windows SSH default shell rather than `cmd.exe`.

Back in an **Administrator PowerShell** on Windows:

```powershell
New-ItemProperty `
    -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH' `
    -Name DefaultShell `
    -Value 'C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe' `
    -PropertyType String `
    -Force
```

No SSH service restart is necessary; this applies to subsequent connections.

Disconnect your Linux SSH session:

```text
exit
```

and reconnect:

```bash
ssh gerit@192.168.178.42
```

You should now land at a PowerShell prompt resembling:

```text
PS C:\Users\gerit>
```

That is the state we want before configuring Ansible.

**So first run these four checks and tell me where you get to:**

```powershell
Get-Service sshd
Test-NetConnection localhost -Port 22
ipconfig
whoami
```

Then from Linux:

```bash
ssh USERNAME@WINDOWS_IP
```
